Before changing project files, read `docs/AI_COORDINATION.md` and the relevant files under `.ai-coordination/`. For a two-laptop task, use `/coordinate-two-laptops` on laptop 1 or `/work-assigned-task` on laptop 2 when available.

Follow the coordination protocol for task assignment, status updates, branch isolation, validation, and handoffs. Laptop 1 is the coordinator and may also implement an independent part of the user's task. Laptop 2 works only on an explicitly assigned task.

When remote-agent session tools are available, check the remote host and live session state before dispatching. A status file is a handoff record, not proof that an agent is idle. Treat unknown or disconnected sessions as busy. Do not create duplicate sessions or poll in a tight loop. Only delegate a clearly independent task within the user's request, with a base commit, ownership boundaries, acceptance criteria, validation, and a stop condition. Otherwise keep working on the main task or ask the user to choose the next task.

Laptop 1 must continue implementing an independent part of the user's request while the worker runs. When either two-laptop prompt is explicitly invoked, the user authorizes automatic checkpoint commits and pushes to each agent's unique task branch only, as described in `docs/AI_COORDINATION.md`. Never force-push, push to the default branch, or auto-merge. Review worker changes before integration. When remote-agent session tools are unavailable, use the inbox/status files and fetch workflow; do not claim that a file update automatically wakes another Copilot session.
